saints.name: St. Eulalia of Mérida
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A young girl of Roman Spain who defied the persecutors of Diocletian and was put to death for confessing Christ…
biography: Eulalia was a Christian girl of Mérida in Roman Spain who, during the persecution of Diocletian about the year 304, presented herself before the magistrate and boldly reproached him for compelling Christians to sacrifice to the gods. Though still very young, she would not yield, and she was tortured and burned to death.
Her memory was cherished throughout Spain and beyond; the poet Prudentius, within a century of her death, sang her passion in one of his hymns, and a great basilica rose over her tomb at Mérida.
saints.knownFor: One of the most celebrated virgin-martyrs of Roman Spain.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
